hypotheses.reasoning: At 02:28:13 session-cache was replaced and came back with 0 keys because no RDB snapshot was found (#115). Until then, logins took 100-150ms. Within a minute, account-svc's cache miss ratio jumped to 95% against a 2% baseline, and it began loading every lookup from accounts-db (#123). That flood of reads pushed accounts-db to 484-493 of 500 connections at 95-98% CPU (#124, #133). Simple primary-key lookups then took 2.7-8.8s (#139, #161, #180), and account-svc queries timed out at 5s (#138, #181). The 504s at edge-proxy (13-26s, from 02:32) are downstream of that. The audit-consumer GC pause at 02:15 came well before the onset and is a red herring. Searches for 'deploy' and 'config' returned nothing.
Another reading of the same lines: accounts-db ran out of CPU and connections. But that overload was caused by the cold cache, not by a leak or by organic growth in traffic.
session-cache may have no persistence/snapshot configured, so a node replacement wipes it. That makes it a possible underlying weakness rather than the trigger.

verdict.recommendedAction: Shed or rate-limit login traffic and add request coalescing (singleflight) for cache fills in account-svc so the cache can warm up without flooding accounts-db. Pre-warm session-cache from accounts-db at a controlled rate. Afterwards, turn on RDB/AOF persistence or replicas for session-cache so a node replacement doesn't come back empty. Also cap how many concurrent DB fallback reads account-svc can make.
